---

**2. PROJECT STATUS UPDATE**

SC opened the item advising the Committee that the overall project status had been formally reviewed with the Client late last week. The project status for Northgate Quay is on_hold as of the last steering committee. Record status: current. SC confirmed this was a current controlled status, not a provisional or draft position, and requested that all reporting and external communications reflect this status until further notice.

The following points were made:

- **Works on site:** JO reported that all active construction works ceased on Monday 29 January. The concrete pour for the Level 2 slab, originally scheduled for 30 January, was cancelled. Plant and equipment have been secured and the site made safe. A full site walkdown was completed on 31 January with the H&S advisor; no significant issues were identified during the shutdown.
- **Design and procurement:** TR confirmed that the structural design package for Levels 3–5 is 92% complete. This work is continuing off-site and is not affected by the on-hold status. Procurement of long-lead steel items is paused; no new orders have been placed since the stop-work instruction.
- **Client position:** AP reiterated that the suspension is to allow a review of the phasing strategy and the interface with the neighbouring highway works. He stated the review is expected to take approximately six weeks, but this is not yet a formal instruction.
- **Comms:** SC to issue a holding statement to the wider project team and subcontractors. The statement is to confirm the suspension and the review period, but not to speculate on a revised completion date at this stage.

**Decision D-2024-014:** The Steering Committee formally ratifies the suspension of all site works at Northgate Quay with immediate effect. The project status is recorded as on_hold in the project control system. The suspension will be reviewed at the next Steering Committee meeting, or earlier if the Client’s review concludes sooner.

**Action A-2024-031:** SC to issue the holding statement to all project stakeholders. Due: 2 February 2024.

AP opened the meeting by confirming that the Client’s phasing review is ongoing. He noted that the six-week period referenced at the last meeting is now nearing its end, and that a formal written instruction is expected within the next 7–10 days.

JW reported that all site works remain suspended. The crane has been parked and will require a full inspection and re-certification before any restart. Scaffolding inspections are being carried out monthly to maintain the safety case, but no access is being permitted above ground floor level.

RB confirmed that the project control system still records the status as on_hold. He has prepared a draft restart programme based on two scenarios (immediate restart vs. four-week notice), but has not yet issued it pending the Client instruction.

**Decision D-2024-015:** The Steering Committee noted the current suspension status and agreed that no site works will resume until the Client issues a formal written instruction. The on_hold status in the project control system is to remain current.

**Action A-2024-032:** RB to update the draft restart programme to include a third scenario (six-week notice) and issue to SC by 05 February 2024 for review.

---

**3. SCHEDULE & COMPLETION DATE**

RB presented the schedule position as at 31 January 2024. He reminded the meeting that the previously approved completion date was 30 June 2025. However, given the suspension and the anticipated duration of the phasing review, the programme has been re-baselined.

RB noted that the re-baselined programme includes the following assumptions:

- Suspension lifted by 15 March 2024 at the latest
- Four-week remobilisation period (including crane inspection, scaffold check, and inductions)
- A 2-week contingency within the programme for weather-related delays during the winter period
- No further changes to the scope of works

JW queried whether the revised date would be sufficient if the suspension were extended beyond March. RB confirmed that the contingency would be consumed, but the date would be at risk. AP stated that the Client is aware of the revised date and is working to the 15 March assumption.

**Action A-2024-033:** RB to issue the re-baselined programme (Rev C) to all attendees and to the Client’s project manager by 02 February 2024.

- Superstructure precast panel design – 70% complete, on track for April issue
- M&E coordination – 60% complete, but noting that the interface with the highway works (under review by Client) may require some re-routing of services

LN raised a concern regarding the cladding package. The specialist subcontractor has indicated that their current quotation will expire on 31 March 2024. If the suspension extends beyond that point, a re-quotation may be required, which could impact the programme and budget.

- **Comms:** SC to issue a holding statement to the wider project team and subcontractors. The statement is to confirm the suspension and the review period, but not to speculate on a revised completion date at this stage.

**2. PROJECT STATUS & SUSPENSION REVIEW**

AP opened the meeting by confirming that the Client’s phasing review is ongoing. He noted that the six-week period referenced at the last meeting is now nearing its end, and that a formal written instruction is expected within the next 7–10 days.

JW reported that all site works remain suspended. The crane has been parked and will require a full inspection and re-certification before any restart. Scaffolding inspections are being carried out monthly to maintain the safety case, but no access is being permitted above ground floor level.

RB confirmed that the project control system still records the status as on_hold. He has prepared a draft restart programme based on two scenarios (immediate restart vs. four-week notice), but has not yet issued it pending the Client instruction.

**Decision D-2024-015:** The Steering Committee noted the current suspension status and agreed that no site works will resume until the Client issues a formal written instruction. The on_hold status in the project control system is to remain current.

**Action A-2024-032:** RB to update the draft restart programme to include a third scenario (six-week notice) and issue to SC by 05 February 2024 for review.

---

**3. SCHEDULE & COMPLETION DATE**

RB presented the schedule position as at 31 January 2024. He reminded the meeting that the previously approved completion date was 30 June 2025. However, given the suspension and the anticipated duration of the phasing review, the programme has been re-baselined.

**Decision D-2024-016:** The Steering Committee reviewed and approved the re-baselined programme. The revised completion date for Northgate Quay is 2025-09-30. Record status: current. This date is now the current controlled completion date in the project control system and will be used for all reporting and contractual purposes.

RB noted that the re-baselined programme includes the following assumptions:

- Suspension lifted by 15 March 2024 at the latest
- Four-week remobilisation period (including crane inspection, scaffold check, and inductions)
- A 2-week contingency within the programme for weather-related delays during the winter period
- No further changes to the scope of works

JW queried whether the revised date would be sufficient if the suspension were extended beyond March. RB confirmed that the contingency would be consumed, but the date would be at risk. AP stated that the Client is aware of the revised date and is working to the 15 March assumption.

**Action A-2024-033:** RB to issue the re-baselined programme (Rev C) to all attendees and to the Client’s project manager by 02 February 2024.

---

**4. DESIGN & PROCUREMENT UPDATE**

LN joined the meeting for this item.

LN reported that design work has continued off-site during the suspension. The following packages are progressing:

- Substructure reinforcement detailing – 95% complete, expected issue for construction by 12 February 2024
- Superstructure precast panel design – 70% complete, on track for April issue
- M&E coordination – 60% complete, but noting that the interface with the highway works (under review by Client) may require some re-routing of services

LN raised a concern regarding the cladding package. The specialist subcontractor has indicated that their current quotation will expire on 31 March 2024. If the suspension extends beyond that point, a re-quotation may be required, which could impact the programme and budget.
